intent: Every gateway event reaches a Rex terminal pane within 1 s p95, and replaying the recorded log rebuilds the FlightLog view exactly (same hash). The pane runs the bun recorder opened with rex split. One line per event: time, session, tool, provider (verified or not), the fence verdict, and the rejection name if there is one.

execution.traffic: Per session: 3 upstream servers register (acme, cloudflare, cloudflare-mcp), then 6 tool calls through the gateway over MCP with 60 to 260 ms between calls: read_document, kv_put to a named target, kv_put to an unnamed target, cloudflare__execute, cloudflare-mcp__execute, kv_delete. No model is involved.
execution.latencyDefinition: paneLatency = the time the polling `rex capture` of the pane returned with the line, minus the event's `at` from the FlightLog row. Poll loop back to back with 10 ms sleep. The capture end time is later than the moment the line was drawn, so the figure is an upper bound. wireLatency = the time the recorder finished writing the line to its stdout, minus `at`.
execution.clock: gateway, recorder and harness run on one machine and share one clock
execution.replay: FlightLog.evolve (the view's own fold) applied to the recorded raw domain events in recorded order, starting from the log state at the cursor where recording began.

amendments.what: Rerun after the gateway capped its events page at 20 (receipts/e3-flight-recorder-before-page-cap.json is the first run, with a page of up to 200). The first run never polled a backlog larger than a few events, so it did not show that a large page hangs. Latency is higher in this run (p95 327 ms against 276 ms) because the local log is larger: each listed event carries the full view state. The starting cursor was 3963 against 2951.

projected.note: Local run: gateway, recorder and pane on one machine. A deployed gateway adds network latency between the gateway and the recorder, and that is not measured here. The recorder reads the gateway with a long poll (FlightLog.list every 50 ms inside the gateway), not a push stream.
notProven: Behaviour when the recorder loses its connection and reconnects.
Throughput above this traffic (about 23 events per session, 4 sessions at once).
That replay would catch a bug in the view's fold, because it runs the same fold. It catches lost, duplicated and reordered events.
